title: Correlation Hopper — Span-Slice Navigator & Timeline Facets
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, keyboard-first drilldown experience for tracing requests that surfaces correlated spans, correlation IDs, and timeline facets without overwhelming the console canvas. The flow should support quick pivoting between related requests, timeline zoom, and span-slice comparison while preserving context for cost/latency analysis.
goals: Enable engineers to identify root-cause spans within 30s for 90% of sampled incidents
Provide an efficient pivoting UX between correlated requests (correlation IDs) and related traces
Support performant rendering for long-span traces (1000+ spans) via progressive disclosure and span slicing
Preserve console patterns (left nav, persistent filters, deep-linkable state) and keyboard accessibility
constraints: Backend returns paginated span windows; design must avoid requiring full-trace load
Memory/CPU on client can be constrained for very large traces; favor virtualized lists
Must interoperate with existing Console filter bar and rollout controls
Timeline must show relative token/latency distribution while meeting 60fps for interactions
user_journeys: Investigate high-latency request: open trace summary, click 'Correlation Hopper' to surface sibling requests and jump to the most relevant span
Compare two spans: select a span slice A, open ephemeral comparison rail, then select span slice B to diff timing and annotations
Filter by correlation ID: apply correlation filter to the workspace then use timeline scrub to see span heatmap for that ID across requests
proposal: Introduce a compact 'Hopper' overlay anchored to the trace timeline. Hopper shows: top correlated requests (by correlation ID), a condensed span map (sparkline heatmap), and 'Span Slice' quick actions (pin, compare, open in full inspector). Timeline supports brush zoom, span level markers, and a focused virtualized list of visible spans. The overlay preserves deep-linkable URL state and exposes keyboard shortcuts (H to open hopper, ←/→ to move between correlated requests).
wireframe_notes: Design uses three horizontal layers: (1) Timeline sparkline with brush; (2) Hopper overlay showing correlated request list and span-slice rail; (3) Bottom ephemeral compare rail that animates open for side-by-side timing comparison. Use muted color tokens for low-signal spans, and a saturated accent for highlighted spans. Keep the main trace canvas visible but dimmed when hopper is active.
accessibility_considerations: Ensure all interactive controls are keyboard focusable and have ARIA labels
Provide text alternatives for timeline sparkline (summary info in tooltip and panel)
Color contrast: heatmap and markers meet WCAG AA against dimmed background
Motion: respect reduced-motion user settings for hover/rail animations
acceptance_criteria: Hopper overlay opens via keyboard shortcut and mouse click; deep-link to a specific correlated request works (URL reflects state)
Timeline brush persists across related request navigation and updates the visible span-slice list
Side-by-side span compare rail supports up to 3 slices and renders within 200ms for traces with 1000 spans (backend pagination respected)
Design assets (Figma frames + prototype) reviewed and approved by PM and Eng; handoff includes tokenized specs
review_feedback: PM (Lina Zhou): emphasize ability to persist selected span as an alert sample for follow-up — add 'Save as Sample' action
Eng (Mateo Gomez): prefer virtualized span list and explicit 'load more' pagination to avoid OOM; check interactions with existing KV cache visualization
Accessibility (Priya Nair): request additional textual summary for sparkline for screen reader users
Design (Jayden Chen): consider compact mode for small screens and collapsed hopper states
decisions: Use virtualized span list with server-side paginated windows rather than client-side full trace expansion
Add 'Save as Sample' action to span quick actions per PM feedback
Expose hopper open/close state in URL to permit deep linking and sharing
Limit side-by-side compare to 3 slices initially; expand later if telemetry supports it
next_steps: Incorporate review feedback and iterate prototype (DES-105433 will track prototype refinements)
Sync with ENG on API contract for paginated span windows (ENG-21512 owner: Mateo)
Create motion spec and reduced-motion variants (estimate 2 points)
Prepare handoff package: annotated frames, tokens, and interaction spec for engineering
